films.title: Foam Festival — Yamuna, 2026
films.logline: Every year during Chhath Puja, thousands wade into the Yamuna at sunrise. Every year, the river is covered in a thick white foam that looks like fresh snow.
synopsis: Every year during Chhath Puja, thousands of devotees wade into the Yamuna in Delhi to offer arghya at sunrise. Every year, the river is covered in a thick white foam that looks like fresh snow.
The photographs are real, and they are taken every November. The film photographs that morning with total reverence, and then tells you what the white is made of.

The froth forms when untreated sewage and detergent runoff load the river with phosphates and surfactants, which whip into foam wherever the water is churned, usually at barrages and weirs. High ammonia is part of the same picture.
In November 2025 the Delhi Pollution Control Committee recorded zero dissolved oxygen at multiple points on the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna. Zero dissolved oxygen means nothing can live there.
The 22 kilometres between Wazirabad and Okhla make up less than two percent of the river's length and carry roughly eighty percent of its pollution load. That stretch is where people stand.
The people in the water did not put any of this in the river.
